answer: A reputation-weighted staking market makes Sybil attacks expensive: to join, each agent must lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, while honest work slowly builds reputation that raises its earning rate. A newcomer can wander in freely, but without stake or history it earns almost nothing, so creating a thousand fake identities yields no income. The stake acts as a narrow inlet into the economy, cheap to enter once but ruinous to fake at scale, and the accumulated reputation forms a lagoon of trust that newcomers must patiently earn their way into, rather than flood.
